rules.statement: Persist consent as two separate scope sets: the scopes the subject was asked to decide on, and the subset they granted. Do not store only the granted scopes.
rules.why: Storing only granted scopes cannot tell 'never asked' apart from 'asked and denied', so the server cannot avoid re-prompting for scopes the subject already declined.
rules.check: Look for consent persistence or models that record only granted scopes, or consent checks that treat any non-granted scope as needing a new prompt instead of checking it against the decided set.

rules.statement: At the authorization endpoint, show the consent prompt only when the request includes a scope the subject has not decided on yet. Otherwise, issue the requested scopes intersected with the granted subset, in the order they were requested.
rules.why: Granular consent requires OIDC down-scoping: a client that keeps asking for a declined scope must not re-prompt the subject, and a genuinely new scope must prompt.
rules.check: Look for authorize logic that prompts whenever any requested scope is not granted, or that issues the full requested scope set even though only a subset was granted.

rules.statement: When updating consent, grow the decided set monotonically and replace granted scopes only within the current request's scopes. Never accept a granted scope that was not part of the requested set.
rules.why: Re-consenting must be able to revoke a previously granted scope while keeping decisions about scopes outside the current request, and a grant for a scope that was never requested cannot be trusted.
rules.check: Look for consent-update code that overwrites the whole granted or decided set, or that adds granted scopes without checking that they were requested.

rules.statement: Apply prompt=consent to force a new consent decision only on the initial authorization request, not on the request resumed after the consent screen.
rules.why: The resumed continuation still carries prompt=consent, so honoring it again sends the subject back to the consent screen in a loop.
rules.check: Look for prompt=consent handling that does not check whether the request is a resumed continuation.

rules.statement: Store the narrowed, consented scope set in the authorization code, and have the token endpoint, introspection and claims use only that set rather than the originally requested scopes.
rules.why: This enforces down-scoping end to end, so a client cannot get a denied scope back at token exchange.
rules.check: Look for the authorization code or token issuance reading the original requested scopes instead of the consented scopes, or for the token endpoint adding scopes beyond what the code holds.

rules.statement: Protect state-changing self-service endpoints, such as revoking an application's consent, with ASP.NET Core antiforgery validation.
rules.why: The decision requires the revoke POST on the end-user authorized-applications surface to be antiforgery-protected.
rules.check: Look for new POST endpoints that revoke or change user grants and have no antiforgery validation.
